title: Data Management — Mission 1: The Prize Wheel Problem
description: The school carnival's prize wheel game is losing money faster than expected. You have one planning session to work out the real odds before opening night.

carla.name: Ms. Carla Nunes
carla.description: Budgets everything down to the last ticket.

prize_table.name: Prize Table
prize_table.description: Lists every prize and how many wedges of the wheel it occupies.

ticket_log.name: Ticket Log
ticket_log.description: Records of how many tickets were sold and prizes given out last year.

elements.text: Last year we gave away more big prizes than the ticket sales could cover. We need the real probabilities before we print the wheel.
Can't we just make the big prize wedge tiny and call it a day?

options.text: "Let's pull the prize table and actually compute the probability of each outcome."
"Just make the wedge look small, nobody's counting."

elements.text: Good, you grabbed the prize table. Let's work the actual numbers.
Eyeballing wedge sizes is how we lost money last year. We need real math.

config.question: The wheel has 20 equal wedges, and 2 of them award the grand prize. What is the probability of landing on the grand prize in one spin?
config.explanation: 2 favorable wedges out of 20 total simplifies to 2/20 = 1/10.

config.prompt: Order these steps for setting fair odds on the wheel, first to last.

items.text: List every possible outcome and its prize
Count favorable outcomes for each prize tier
Divide favorable outcomes by total outcomes
Check the resulting probabilities against the prize budget

config.prompt: Ozzy: "If 4 volunteers sign up and we need to pick 2 to run the wheel, how many different pairs are possible? Just the number."

elements.text: The odds are set and the budget checks out. We're ready to open.
We'll open, but the budget's tight. Next time, compute the odds before touching the wheel.

elements.prompt: The wheel is printed. What now?

options.text: Show Ozzy how to compute probability and combinations for any game.
Log off. The wheel's printed, that's enough for today.

elements.text: So probability isn't vibes, it's just favorable outcomes over total outcomes. I can work with that.

ending.title: Probability Hero
ending.description: Fixed the prize wheel's odds and taught the team how to calculate them.

ending.title: Wheel Printed
ending.description: The wheel is ready. The deeper lesson can wait until tomorrow.
